what: On a paper ground the cursor leaves halftone marks — on a 1/8 resolution trail grid (Float32 math over a 2D canvas) it stamps where the cursor passed like brush strokes (strength = Pixels moved ÷ 15 (max 1) × .1, radius .085 × (1 + strength × 1.5) — the faster the move, the thicker and darker the mark, and .65 longer in the direction of movement. Each frame it blends .6 with its four neighbors to spread, and decays by .94. The trail is stamped as a 6px cell halftone, with each cell having its own random threshold, so only cells where trail strength × 1.5 exceeds the threshold turn on. The darker the trail, the denser the loose cluster of dots (diameter .44~.68 of the cell, text color at .4 transparency). On press, a ring spreads from that spot (radius +.012 per frame, strength ×.93) and sweeps the halftone away.

options.radius: Brush radius (ratio to panel height), default .085
options.force: Force (px of one cursor move ÷ 15, max 1) × this value = Intensity stamped per frame, default .1
options.gain: Threshold multiplier at which dots light up — larger means more dots even on faint marks, default 1.5

use: — The dot color is that element’s color, if the skin was changed, el.dispatchEvent(new Event('fx:repaint'))
note: The original draws paper grain (fibers, creases, stains, wrinkles) with a WebGL2 shader, and marks spread following that grain. This part ports only the same mark computation (1/8 cell · neighbor .6 mix · .94 decay · stretched brush stroke) plus halftone and press ring to a 2D canvas. It draws on any device and pauses drawing once the marks have fully faded. Paper grain is left to the host background (grain canvas etc.).

from.where: Background of every page .co-paper — the cursor trail (wake dot plume) from the original canvas.paper-gl
